havilah_1461.name: Havilah
havilah_1461.who: A son of Cush, grandson of Ham, listed in the Table of Nations after the flood.
key: Havilah is named among the sons of Cush, alongside Seba, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Cush's sons in its genealogy from Adam (1 Chronicles 1).

havilah_1462.name: Havilah
havilah_1462.who: A son of Joktan in Shem's line through Eber, listed in the Table of Nations.
key: Havilah is named among the thirteen sons of Joktan, with Ophir and Jobab (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Joktan's sons in the line of Shem (1 Chronicles 1).

heber_1470.name: Heber
heber_1470.who: A Kenite, descended from Moses' in-law Hobab, and the husband of Jael, who killed Sisera.
key: Heber separated from the other Kenites and pitched his tent near Kedesh (Judges 4).
His household was at peace with Jabin king of Hazor (Judges 4).
So the fleeing Sisera came to the tent of Heber's wife Jael, who killed him (Judges 4).
Deborah's song blesses Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite (Judges 5).

heleb_1480.name: Heleb
heleb_1480.who: A warrior from Netophah, son of Baanah, counted among David's mighty men.
key: Heleb son of Baanah of Netophah is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles' list of David's mighty men names him Heled (1 Chronicles 11).
Heldai the Netophathite, probably the same man, commanded the army division for the twelfth month (1 Chronicles 27).

herodias_1507.name: Herodias
herodias_1507.who: Wife of Herod Antipas, formerly married to his brother Philip, who brought about John the Baptist's death.
key: John the Baptist rebuked Herod for marrying Herodias, his brother Philip's wife (Luke 3).
Herod imprisoned John for her sake, and she held a grudge, wanting him killed (Mark 6).
When her daughter pleased Herod with a dance, Herodias told her to ask for John's head (Mark 6).
Herod reluctantly had John beheaded, and the head was brought to her (Matthew 14).

hezekiah_1513.name: Hizkiah
hezekiah_1513.who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, son of Neariah; not King Hezekiah.
key: He is listed as a son of Neariah, with his brothers Elioenai and Azrikam (1 Chronicles 3).
His family belongs to the line of David's descendants recorded after the exile (1 Chronicles 3).

hiel_1522.name: Hiel
hiel_1522.who: A man of Bethel who rebuilt Jericho during King Ahab's reign, at the cost of two sons.
key: In Ahab's days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt the city of Jericho (1 Kings 16).
He laid its foundation at the cost of his firstborn Abiram and set its gates at the cost of Segub (1 Kings 16).
This fulfilled the curse Joshua spoke over anyone who would rebuild Jericho (1 Kings 16; Joshua 6).

hilkiah_1525.name: Hilkiah
hilkiah_1525.who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, ancestor of Ethan the singer; not the high priest Hilkiah.
key: He is listed as son of Amzi and father of Amaziah in the Merarite line (1 Chronicles 6).
His descendant Ethan was among the singers David appointed for the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 6).

hobab_1537.name: Hobab
hobab_1537.who: A Midianite, son of Reuel and relative of Moses by marriage, whom Moses asked to guide Israel.
key: As Israel set out from Sinai, Moses invited Hobab to come and share the LORD's good (Numbers 10).
Hobab at first declined, wishing to return to his own land and kindred (Numbers 10).
Moses urged him to stay, since he knew where to camp and could serve as Israel's eyes (Numbers 10).
Later Heber the Kenite is described as a descendant of Hobab, Moses' in-law (Judges 4).

horam_1551.name: Horam
horam_1551.who: A Canaanite king of Gezer defeated by Joshua during the southern campaign.
key: Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish while Joshua was attacking it (Joshua 10).
Joshua struck him and his people until none remained (Joshua 10).

hori_1552.name: Hori
hori_1552.who: A son of Lotan, from the Horite clans living in Seir, the land later held by Esau's descendants.
key: Hori is listed with Hemam as the sons of Lotan, whose sister was Timna (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

hosea_1555.name: Hosea
hosea_1555.who: A prophet to Israel's northern kingdom whose marriage to unfaithful Gomer pictured God's love for unfaithful Israel.
key: He prophesied in the days of Uzziah through Hezekiah of Judah and Jeroboam of Israel (Hosea 1).
God commanded him to marry Gomer, a picture of Israel forsaking the LORD (Hosea 1).
Their children Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, and Lo-ammi were given names announcing judgment on Israel (Hosea 1).
God told him to love his wife again, and he bought her back (Hosea 3).
Paul cites Hosea's promise that those not God's people would be called his people (Romans 9).

hotham_1562.name: Hotham
hotham_1562.who: A man of the tribe of Asher, son of Heber and grandson of Beriah.
key: He is listed with Japhlet, Shomer, and their sister Shua as the sons of Heber (1 Chronicles 7).
Asher's descendants were heads of fathers' houses, choice men, and mighty warriors (1 Chronicles 7).

huldah_1567.name: Huldah
huldah_1567.who: A prophetess in Jerusalem whom King Josiah consulted after the Book of the Law was found.
key: She lived in Jerusalem's Second Quarter and was the wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe (2 Kings 22).
Josiah sent Hilkiah the priest and others to her to inquire about the newly found book (2 Kings 22).
She declared that the disaster written in the book would come upon Jerusalem (2 Kings 22).
Because Josiah humbled himself, she said he would not see the disaster himself (2 Kings 22).
Chronicles records the same message, after which Josiah led Judah in renewing the covenant (2 Chronicles 34).

hurai_1521.name: Hurai
hurai_1521.who: A warrior from the brooks of Gaash, counted among David's mighty men.
key: Samuel's list of David's mighty men names him Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles' list of the same mighty men calls him Hurai (1 Chronicles 11).

huram_1575.name: Huram
huram_1575.who: Dataset mis-entry from the KJV phrase 'Huram my father's'; modern Bibles read Huram-abi, the craftsman Hiram.

hymenaeus_1583.name: Hymenaeus
hymenaeus_1583.who: A false teacher in the church whom Paul warned Timothy about for abandoning the faith.
key: Having rejected faith and a good conscience, he made shipwreck of his faith (1 Timothy 1).
Paul handed him and Alexander over to Satan so they would learn not to blaspheme (1 Timothy 1).
With Philetus he taught that the resurrection had already happened, upsetting some believers' faith (2 Timothy 2).

ibzan_1588.name: Ibzan
ibzan_1588.who: A judge of Israel from Bethlehem who led Israel for seven years after Jephthah.
key: Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel after Jephthah (Judges 12).
He had thirty sons and thirty daughters, arranging marriages for them outside his clan (Judges 12).
He judged Israel seven years, then died and was buried at Bethlehem (Judges 12).

iddo_1595.name: Iddo
iddo_1595.who: A priest who returned from exile, the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah.
key: An Iddo is listed among the priests who came up from exile with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12).
Ezra calls the prophet Zechariah his son, naming him by his grandfather (Ezra 5).
Through the preaching of Zechariah the son of Iddo, the elders finished building the temple (Ezra 6).
Zechariah's book names him son of Berechiah, son of Iddo (Zechariah 1).

igal_1599.name: Igal
igal_1599.who: A warrior from Zobah, son of Nathan, counted among David's mighty men.
key: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Zobah was an Aramean kingdom that David had earlier defeated (2 Samuel 8).

iscah_618.name: Iscah
iscah_618.who: A daughter of Haran, niece of Abram, and sister of Lot and Milcah.
key: She was a daughter of Haran, Abram's brother, who died in Ur (Genesis 11).
She is named when her uncle Nahor married her sister Milcah (Genesis 11).

ishbi-benob_621.name: Ishbi-benob
ishbi-benob_621.who: A Philistine warrior descended from the giants who tried to kill David in battle.
key: Armed with a new sword and a heavy bronze spear, he thought to kill a weary David (2 Samuel 21).
Abishai son of Zeruiah came to David's aid and killed him (2 Samuel 21).
Afterward David's men swore he would no longer go out with them to battle (2 Samuel 21).

jabez_675.name: Jabez
jabez_675.who: A man listed among Judah's descendants, more honorable than his brothers, whose prayer God answered.
key: He was more honorable than his brothers, and his mother named him for bearing him in pain (1 Chronicles 4).
He called on God to bless him, enlarge his border, and keep him from harm (1 Chronicles 4).
God granted what he asked (1 Chronicles 4).

jabin_676.name: Jabin
jabin_676.who: A Canaanite king of Hazor who led the northern kings against Joshua and was killed.
key: Hearing of Israel's victories, Jabin summoned the kings of the north to fight Israel (Joshua 11).
Their great army, with many horses and chariots, camped at the waters of Merom (Joshua 11).
The LORD gave them into Israel's hand, and Joshua routed them (Joshua 11).
Joshua captured Hazor, struck its king with the sword, and burned the city (Joshua 11).

jacob_683.name: Jacob
jacob_683.who: Son of Matthan and father of Joseph, Mary's husband, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus; not the patriarch.
key: Matthew lists him as son of Matthan in the royal line descended from David (Matthew 1).
He was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born (Matthew 1).

jahaziel_698.name: Jahaziel
jahaziel_698.who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, the third son of Hebron.
key: He is listed as Hebron's third son in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His name appears again among the Levite families assigned by lot for service (1 Chronicles 24).

jahaziel_699.name: Jahaziel
jahaziel_699.who: A Levite of the sons of Asaph who prophesied victory to King Jehoshaphat facing a vast invading army.
key: As Judah gathered to pray, the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel in the assembly (2 Chronicles 20).
He told them not to fear, for the battle was not theirs but God's (2 Chronicles 20).
He said they would not need to fight, only stand firm and see the LORD's salvation (2 Chronicles 20).
Jehoshaphat and the people bowed in worship, and the next day the enemies destroyed one another (2 Chronicles 20).

jair_708.name: Jair
jair_708.who: A descendant of Manasseh who captured villages east of the Jordan and named them Havvoth-jair.
key: Jair son of Manasseh captured villages in Gilead and called them Havvoth-jair (Numbers 32).
He took the whole region of Argob in Bashan and named it after himself (Deuteronomy 3).
Under Solomon, the villages of Jair in Gilead belonged to a district officer's territory (1 Kings 4).
Chronicles traces him through Segub, son of Hezron, and says he held twenty-three cities in Gilead (1 Chronicles 2).

jair_709.name: Jair
jair_709.who: A Gileadite who judged Israel for twenty-two years after Tola.
key: After Tola, Jair the Gileadite judged Israel twenty-two years (Judges 10).
His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys and had thirty cities in Gilead called Havvoth-jair (Judges 10).
He died and was buried in Kamon (Judges 10).

jairus_711.name: Jairus
jairus_711.who: A synagogue ruler whose twelve-year-old daughter Jesus raised from the dead.
key: Jairus fell at Jesus' feet, begging him to come heal his dying daughter (Mark 5).
On the way, Jesus stopped to speak with a woman healed of a bleeding disorder (Mark 5).
When word came that the girl had died, Jesus told Jairus not to fear, only believe (Mark 5).
Jesus took her by the hand and she rose, and he told them to give her food (Luke 8).

japhlet_729.name: Japhlet
japhlet_729.who: A man of the tribe of Asher, son of Heber and grandson of Beriah.
key: He is listed with Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua as the sons of Heber (1 Chronicles 7).
His sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath (1 Chronicles 7).

jehiel_771.name: Jehiel
jehiel_771.who: A Gershonite Levite, chief of the sons of Ladan, whose family oversaw the temple treasuries.
key: He is named chief among the sons of Ladan in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His family was put in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26).
Leaders' gifts of precious stones were given into the treasury in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite (1 Chronicles 29).

jehoiada_794.name: Jehoiada
jehoiada_794.who: Son of Benaiah, one of King David's counselors after Ahithophel.
key: Jehoiada son of Benaiah succeeded Ahithophel as a counselor to King David (1 Chronicles 27).
He served alongside Abiathar, while Joab commanded the king's army (1 Chronicles 27).

jehoshabeath_811.name: Jehosheba
jehoshabeath_811.who: A daughter of King Jehoram and wife of the priest Jehoiada, who saved young Joash from Athaliah.
key: When Athaliah destroyed the royal family, Jehosheba stole away her nephew Joash, son of Ahaziah (2 Kings 11).
She hid him and his nurse in a bedroom so he was not killed (2 Kings 11).
Joash stayed hidden with her in the house of the LORD for six years (2 Kings 11).
Chronicles adds that she was the wife of Jehoiada the priest (2 Chronicles 22).

jehoshaphat_806.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat_806.who: Son of Ahilud, the royal recorder under King David and King Solomon.
key: Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud served as recorder among David's officials (2 Samuel 8).
He is again listed as recorder after David's return to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 20).
He continued as recorder among Solomon's high officials (1 Kings 4).
Chronicles lists him as recorder in David's reign (1 Chronicles 18).

jehoshaphat_807.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat_807.who: Son of Paruah, one of King Solomon's twelve district officers, over Issachar.
key: Solomon's twelve officers each supplied food for the king's household one month a year (1 Kings 4).
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah served as the officer over Issachar (1 Kings 4).

jehoshaphat_809.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat_809.who: Son of Nimshi and father of Jehu, who became king of Israel.
key: Elisha sent a young prophet to anoint Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi (2 Kings 9).
His son Jehu conspired against King Joram and seized Israel's throne (2 Kings 9).

jekameam_834.name: Jekameam
jekameam_834.who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, the fourth son of Hebron.
key: He is listed as Hebron's fourth son in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His name appears again among the Levite families assigned by lot for service (1 Chronicles 24).

jeremiah_848.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah_848.who: A man of Libnah, grandfather of Kings Jehoahaz and Zedekiah through his daughter Hamutal; not the prophet.
key: His daughter Hamutal was the mother of King Jehoahaz of Judah (2 Kings 23).
Hamutal was also the mother of Zedekiah, Judah's last king (2 Kings 24).
The book of Jeremiah repeats that Zedekiah's mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah (Jeremiah 52).

jeremiah_855.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah_855.who: A Rechabite, son of Habazziniah and father of Jaazaniah; not the prophet Jeremiah.
key: The prophet Jeremiah brought his son Jaazaniah and the Rechabites into the temple and offered them wine (Jeremiah 35).
They refused, obeying their ancestor Jonadab, and the LORD promised their line would endure (Jeremiah 35).

jeremoth_857.name: Jeremoth
jeremoth_857.who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, son of Mushi.
key: He is listed with Mahli and Eder as the sons of Mushi in David's Levite organization (1 Chronicles 23).
His name appears again among the Levite families assigned by lot for service (1 Chronicles 24).

jeriah_860.name: Jeriah
jeriah_860.who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, the chief among the sons of Hebron.
key: He is listed as the chief of Hebron's sons in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His name appears again among the Levite families assigned by lot for service (1 Chronicles 24).

jeshua_894.name: Jeshua
jeshua_894.who: Head of a family within the clan of Pahath-moab whose descendants returned from exile with Zerubbabel.
key: His descendants, with Joab's, were counted among the sons of Pahath-moab, numbering 2,812 (Ezra 2).
Nehemiah's copy of the list gives 2,818 for the same families (Nehemiah 7).

jeshua_898.name: Jeshua
jeshua_898.who: A chief of the Levites after the exile, son of Kadmiel, who led praise and thanksgiving.
key: Jeshua son of Kadmiel is named among the chiefs of the Levites (Nehemiah 12).
With their brothers they stood in sections to praise and give thanks, as David commanded (Nehemiah 12).

jeshua_899.name: Jeshua
jeshua_899.who: The high priest, son of Jozadak, who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and helped rebuild the temple.
key: He was among the leaders who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
He and his fellow priests rebuilt the altar and began laying the temple's foundation (Ezra 3).
With Zerubbabel he refused the adversaries' offer to help build (Ezra 4).
Called Joshua, he was stirred by Haggai's message to resume work on the temple (Haggai 1).
Some of his descendants later pledged to put away their foreign wives (Ezra 10).

jeush_913.name: Jeush
jeush_913.who: A son of Esau and Oholibamah, born in Canaan, who became a chief in Edom.
key: Oholibamah bore Jeush to Esau in Canaan, along with Jalam and Korah (Genesis 36).
He became one of the chiefs descended from Esau (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among Esau's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

jezreel_1613.name: Jezreel
jezreel_1613.who: The first son of the prophet Hosea and Gomer, whose name announced judgment and later restoration.
key: Gomer bore Hosea a son, and the LORD told him to name the boy Jezreel (Hosea 1).
The name announced punishment on Jehu's house for the blood shed at Jezreel (Hosea 1).
God promised a great day of Jezreel when Judah and Israel would be gathered together (Hosea 1).
The name later becomes a promise of blessing, as God sows his people in the land (Hosea 2).

jobab_1641.name: Jobab
jobab_1641.who: An early king of Edom, son of Zerah of Bozrah, who reigned before Israel had kings.
key: Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in Edom after Bela died (Genesis 36).
When Jobab died, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him in its list of Edom's kings (1 Chronicles 1).

jochebed_1645.name: Jochebed
jochebed_1645.who: A daughter of Levi, wife of Amram, and mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
key: As Moses' mother, she hid her baby for three months from Pharaoh's decree (Exodus 2).
She placed him in a basket among the reeds by the Nile (Exodus 2).
Pharaoh's daughter then paid her to nurse her own son (Exodus 2).
The genealogy names her Jochebed, Amram's wife and his father's sister (Exodus 6).
She is called Levi's daughter, born in Egypt, mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam (Numbers 26).

joel_1647.name: Joel
joel_1647.who: Samuel's firstborn son, a corrupt judge in Beersheba, and grandfather of the singer Heman's line.
key: Samuel appointed his sons Joel and Abijah as judges in Beersheba (1 Samuel 8).
They turned aside after gain, took bribes, and perverted justice (1 Samuel 8).
Their corruption led Israel's elders to ask Samuel for a king (1 Samuel 8).
His son Heman became a leading singer when David organized worship (1 Chronicles 6).
Heman son of Joel sounded bronze cymbals when the ark was brought up (1 Chronicles 15).

joel_1655.name: Joel
joel_1655.who: A Gershonite Levite of the family of Ladan who helped oversee the temple treasuries.
key: He is listed with Jehiel and Zetham among the sons of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23).
With his brother Zetham he was in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26).

joel_1660.name: Joel
joel_1660.who: A prophet, son of Pethuel, who used a locust plague to call Judah to repentance.
key: The word of the LORD came to Joel son of Pethuel (Joel 1).
He called priests and people to mourn and fast after a devastating locust plague (Joel 1).
He warned of the day of the LORD and urged Judah to return with all their heart (Joel 2).
He announced God's promise to pour out his Spirit on all flesh (Joel 2).
At Pentecost, Peter declared that this outpouring fulfilled Joel's prophecy (Acts 2).
